claims.text: Combining adaptive bias force or metadynamics with a machine-learning potential will substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method will maintain fidelity relative to explicit ab initio results.
Advanced sampling will improve the efficiency of free-energy calculations.
Advanced sampling will accurately capture the free-energy landscape.
The proposed method will retain vibrational-entropy contributions.
The proposed method will retain anharmonic contributions.
The proposed method will retain electron–vibration coupling.
A machine-learning potential will provide an accurate representation of the potential-energy surface.
Accurate representation of the potential-energy surface is essential for calculating solid- and fluid-state free energies and the relevant entropy terms.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by 55–65% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will improve throughput by 25–35% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will achieve 96–99% fidelity relative to explicit ab initio results.
The proposed method is intended to apply to high-entropy systems containing 3–6 principal elements.
The proposed temperature domain is 500–2500 K.
Systems containing 3–6 principal elements are representative of many high-entropy systems.
The 500–2500 K interval captures a wide range of high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
Accuracy may vary with the specific high-entropy system and the performance of the machine-learning potential and sampling method.
Computational cost and throughput may depend on system complexity and available computational resources.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if phase-free-energy and derived-observable differences exceed 2% in more than 80% of test cases relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
